According to the latest report by Counterpoint Research, despite the broader industry downturn, Apple's iPhone shipments still grew 3% year-on-year, reaching a record-high 20% share of global smartphone shipments. Here are the details.

The lowest level for a second quarter since 2013

Counterpoint Research said that during the second quarter of 2026, Samsung led the global smartphone market with a 24% shipment share, followed closely by Apple at 20% (a record high for that period), Xiaomi at 12%, OPPO at 11%, and vivo at 8%.

Compared with the same period last year, Samsung's market share rose by four percentage points, Apple by three, and vivo by one, while Xiaomi fell by two and OPPO by one. The combined share of other manufacturers dropped from 28% to 26%.

Counterpoint noted that Samsung returned to the top of the global smartphone sell-in rankings in the second quarter of 2026, after Apple had led in the first quarter on the back of strong demand for the iPhone 17.

As for the second quarter of 2026, although Apple was the only major OEM not to raise prices, Samsung benefited from strong demand for the Galaxy S26 series, improved product availability, and a more aggressive promotional strategy, growing at a faster pace.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects "global smartphone shipments for the full year to fall by roughly 14%, with the global memory shortage expected to persist into 2027." The firm noted that until supply conditions improve, manufacturers will continue to trim low-margin models, adjust storage configurations, and rely more heavily on refurbished and previous-generation products.
